options.why: Sand is in some soils, but soil also has humus, air and water.

options.text: tiny bits of rock mixed with rotted plants and animals

options.why: Plastic is not a natural part of soil.
Rotted leaves are part of soil, but it also has tiny bits of rock.

hints: Soil has more than one ingredient.
Some of it comes from rock broken into tiny pieces.
The rest comes from things that were once alive.
items.explanation: Soil is made of tiny bits of rock mixed with humus, which is rotted plant and animal material. Soil also holds air and water.

items.prompt: The dark part of soil made from rotted plants and animals is called ___.
hints: It makes soil dark and rich.
Gardeners like soil with lots of it.
The word has five letters and starts with h.
items.explanation: Humus is rotted plant and animal material. It makes soil dark and gives plants minerals.

items.prompt: Which of these is a fossil?

options.text: a shell on the beach today
options.why: A fossil comes from a living thing that died very long ago, kept in rock.
A pebble is a rock, but it shows no living thing.

options.text: the shape of an ancient shell kept in rock

options.why: A toy is made by people. It is not a fossil.

hints: Fossils come from living things.
Fossils are found in rock.
They are very, very old.
items.explanation: A fossil is the remains or shape of a living thing from very long ago, kept in rock.

items.prompt: Put the steps of how a fossil forms in order.
items: A sea animal dies and sinks to the seabed.
Mud and sand quickly cover its body.
The soft parts rot, leaving the hard shell or bones.
More layers press down and slowly turn into rock.
Over a very long time, the rock wears away and the fossil is found.
hints: The animal must die first.
It needs to be buried before it can become part of a rock.
Being found by people comes last.
items.explanation: A buried animal's soft parts rot away, and its hard parts are pressed in layers that become rock. Much later, the rock wears away and the fossil appears.

items.prompt: Asha scratches four rocks with an iron nail. Which rock is the hardest?

head: Rock
Scratched by the nail?
figure.alt: Table of a scratch test: chalk was scratched easily, sandstone was scratched, marble was scratched a little, granite was not scratched.

options.why: Chalk was scratched easily, so it is the softest.
Sandstone was scratched, so it is quite soft.
Marble was scratched a little, so it is not the hardest.

hints: A hard rock is difficult to scratch.
Look for the rock the nail could not scratch.
Read the second column carefully.
items.explanation: The nail could not scratch granite, so granite is the hardest. Chalk was scratched easily, so it is the softest.

items.prompt: Drops of water were put on four rocks. Which rock would make the best roof?

head: Rock
Did the water soak in?
figure.alt: Table: water soaked into chalk, sandstone and pumice. Water did not soak into slate.

options.why: Water soaked into chalk, so rain would get through.
Water soaked into sandstone.
Pumice is full of holes, and water soaked in.

hints: A roof must keep rain out.
Look for the rock where water did not soak in.
Read the second column for each rock.
items.explanation: Water did not soak into slate, so slate keeps rain out. Slate also splits into thin, flat sheets, which make good roof tiles.

items.prompt: Which soil lets water drain through it fastest?

options.why: Clay has tiny, tightly packed bits, so water drains slowly.

options.text: soil packed hard on a path
options.why: Packed soil has few gaps, so water drains slowly.

options.text: all soils drain at the same speed
options.why: Different soils drain at very different speeds.

hints: Water drains through gaps between the bits of soil.
Big grains leave big gaps.
Which soil has the biggest grains?
items.explanation: Sandy soil has big grains with big gaps between them. Water runs through the gaps quickly.

items.prompt: Each soil had 100 ml of water poured on it. How much water stayed in the clay soil?

head: Soil
Water that drained through (ml)
figure.alt: Table: 100 ml of water was poured on each soil. 80 ml drained through sandy soil, 50 ml through garden soil and 15 ml through clay soil.

hints: 100 ml went in at the top.
Find how much came out of the clay soil.
The rest stayed in the soil. Take it away from 100.
items.explanation: 15 ml drained through the clay, so 100 take away 15 is 85 ml. Clay soil holds on to lots of water.

items.prompt: Pumice is a rock from volcanoes. It is full of tiny air holes. What happens when you put it in water?

options.why: Pumice is full of trapped air, which makes it light enough to float.
Pumice is a rock. It does not dissolve in water.
Rocks do not melt in water.

hints: Think about the tiny air holes.
Things full of air are very light for their size.
Would a light, airy rock sink or stay on top?
items.explanation: Pumice is full of trapped air, so it floats. Volcanoes in Indonesia have made large rafts of floating pumice.

items.prompt: In which kind of rock are fossils most often found?

options.text: rock that was once melted, like granite
options.why: Melted rock is far too hot. It would destroy any remains.
Glass is not a rock. It is made by heating sand.
The Moon has no living things, so it has no fossils.

options.text: rock made from layers of mud and sand

hints: Fossils form when living things are buried.
What buries a dead sea animal on the seabed?
Which rock is made from those layers?
items.explanation: Fossils are found in sedimentary rock. It forms from layers of mud and sand that bury living things.

items.prompt: Which part of an animal is most likely to become a fossil?

options.why: Soft parts usually rot before they can become fossils.
Eyes are soft and rot quickly.
Fur rots away quickly.

hints: Fossils take a very long time to form.
Soft parts rot quickly.
Which parts are the hardest?
items.explanation: Hard parts such as bones, teeth and shells last much longer than soft parts. So they are most likely to become fossils.

items.prompt: Fossils of sea shells are found in rock at the top of a high mountain. What does this tell us?

options.text: Sea animals used to climb mountains.
options.why: Shellfish cannot climb mountains.

options.text: The rock was once under the sea.

options.why: The fossils are inside the rock, so they were buried as the rock formed.
Sea shells come from sea animals.

hints: Where did the shell animals live?
The fossils are inside the rock itself.
Where must the rock have formed?
items.explanation: The shells were buried as the rock formed under the sea. Over a very long time, the rock was pushed up to make a mountain.
